chapter: Roosevelt jazz sessions and Charlie Parker
title: Bird's first appearance at Roosevelt and the wire recording
summary: A mix-up over Charlie Ventura's booking leads to Charlie Parker playing the school; a wire recording is made.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And no, these guys would come on their off night like Monday or Tuesday would be an off night. They’d come up in the early evening before they went to work and so forth. Actually the first time Bird came up was sort of a mistake. Some fraternity or social club had booked Charlie Ventura who was hot then for their dance at the school. But Charlie had just finished a week at the Chicago Theater, and the union had a rule that you couldn’t play another gig for a period of time in town. And it so happened that Bird’s manager was up at the booking office at the time, so he said “well, let’s give Bird the gig.” So they didn’t know one Charlie from another anyhow. But we put out calls to all the Bird fans. We couldn’t get too many of them there, but he came up with his full band
I don’t know if it was Al Hagert, Duke Jordan, you know. It was one of those groups.
Maybe Stan Levey? I don’t know. Stan was with him at that time.
No, no. It was probably Max.

In just a few weeks we got a wire recording - that’s how early it was - it was still wire recordings, but his manager wouldn’t let us record anymore. Bird said it was ok, but he said no, he cut it down.
So do you still have that? Is that?
